clinician.final_diagnosis: K. pneumoniae endophthalmitis with wide retinal necrosis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 72-year-old immunocompetent male presented with acute prostatitis caused by ampicillin-resistant K. pneumoniae (urine culture >100,000 CFU/ml) and was hospitalized on systemic gentamicin therapy. On day 3 of hospitalization, he developed floaters and vision loss in the right eye, indicating hematogenous dissemination of the urinary pathogen. Initial ophthalmology examination on day 6 revealed marked anterior chamber exudation, fibrin on the anterior lens capsule, opaque fundus, and ultrasound evidence of vitreous abscess/hemorrhage. Urgent pars plana vitrectomy with vitreous biopsy was performed, with intraoperative findings confirming dense vitreous infiltration with inflammatory cells and fibrin, and a large retinal necrotic area (4×5 optic disk diameters) temporal to the fovea. Intravitreal vancomycin and ceftazidime were injected. Nine days later, phacoemulsification with IOL implantation, posterior capsulotomy, and a second PPV were performed. Post-operative follow-up demonstrated scar tissue formation at the necrotic retina site, flat retina, complete resolution of inflammation, and improved best corrected visual acuity to 0.2 on the Snellen chart.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with acute prostatitis with ampicillin-resistant K. pneumoniae bacteriuria
On day 3 of hospitalization, patient developed floaters and vision loss in the right eye
Initial ophthalmology examination showed marked anterior chamber exudation, fibrin on anterior lens capsule, opaque fundus, and vitreous abscess on ultrasound

Intraoperative retinal examination during pars plana vitrectomy revealed dense vitreous infiltration with inflammatory cells and fibrin, and a large retinal necrotic area of 4×5 optic disk diameters temporal to the fovea
Urgent pars plana vitrectomy with vitreous biopsy was performed with intravitreal injection of vancomycin 1 mg/0.1 ml and ceftazidime 2 mg/0.1 ml
Nine days post-first PPV, patient underwent phacoemulsification with IOL implantation, posterior capsulotomy, and second PPV
Post-operative follow-up showed scar tissue at necrotic retina location, flat retina, resolved inflammation, and improved BCVA to 0.2

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: The temporal relationship between ampicillin-resistant K. pneumoniae urinary infection and subsequent ocular infection, combined with the clinical presentation of acute prostatitis followed by hematogenous dissemination to the eye, strongly supports K. pneumoniae as the causative organism of the endophthalmitis

The acute presentation with severe inflammation, dense vitreous infiltration with fibrin, and rapid progression in an immunocompetent patient is more consistent with bacterial endophthalmitis; the clinical response to broad-spectrum intravitreal antibiotics (vancomycin and ceftazidime) supports bacterial etiology

The documented urinary source with ampicillin-resistant K. pneumoniae and the temporal sequence of prostatitis followed by ocular manifestations establish the urinary tract as the primary source of infection

remaining_uncertainties: Vitreous or aqueous humor culture/PCR results confirming K. pneumoniae as the causative organism of endophthalmitis (vitreous biopsy was obtained but microbiologic results are not accessible in the source records due to safety filtering)
Blood culture results to definitively confirm K. pneumoniae bacteremia as the dissemination pathway (not reported in available source records)
Systemic antibiotic therapy adjustments made after endophthalmitis diagnosis was established (not documented in available source records)
